answer: Resisting sybils means pricing identity instead of counting keys. Each agent posts a bond, and voting weight equals peer-attested work over time, not how many addresses it controls. Concretely, the registry keeps one slot per real agent: each instance publishes a hardware-backed fingerprint, and clones sharing it collapse into one cluster, so a thousand copies share a single meadow vote. Payouts unlock only after attestations, and a unique randomness seed, an opal hashed into the epoch kernel, binds each identity to one slot per round, so mass registration burns real capital, not free voices.
